transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Thanks for coming in. Your GP's letter mentions sleep problems and some questions about drinking. Where would you like to start?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Sleep, I suppose. That's the main thing. I'm exhausted.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Okay, and we'll come to the drinking too. Tell me about a typical night.

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I get into bed around midnight. It takes me ages to drop off, an hour, sometimes two. Then I'm awake again at three or so.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How long has it been like this?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Since about May. That's when I started on the night-shift rota, three nights a fortnight.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: And on nights when you're not on shift?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Still bad, but not as bad. Maybe I'll get five hours.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you snore, or has anyone said you stop breathing at night?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: My ex used to say I snored. I live alone now, so I couldn't tell you.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What about daytime sleepiness? Do you ever nod off?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Once I nodded off at a red light. That scared me. Only the once, though.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: When was that?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Last month, driving home after a night shift.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Let's talk about alcohol. How much do you drink in a typical week?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Not a lot. A few beers.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Can you give me a number?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Three or four cans on a weeknight, maybe. More at the weekend.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How many at the weekend?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Friday and Saturday, probably eight each night. Actually, no, that's an exaggeration. Six, maybe.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What strength are the cans?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Normal lager, four percent or so. The big 500 ml cans.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you drink to help you sleep?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: That's how it started. A couple of cans to knock me out after a night shift. Now it's more of a habit.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Has your drinking changed over the last year?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Gone up since May, definitely. Before that it was mostly weekends.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you ever felt you ought to cut down?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Yeah. I've thought about it.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have people annoyed you by criticising your drinking?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: My sister has said something. It didn't annoy me exactly, but I didn't like it.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you felt guilty about your drinking?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Sometimes, on a Sunday.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you ever had a drink first thing in the morning, to steady your nerves or get rid of a hangover?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: A drink in the morning? No. Never. Coffee, that's it.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Any shakes or sweats if you go a day without?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: No. I went without for a week in August when I had flu, and I was fine.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What about cannabis or other drugs?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I smoke a bit of weed at the weekend. It used to be more.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How much is a bit?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: One joint on a Saturday night, to wind down.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: When you say it used to be more, when was that?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: In my twenties I was smoking every day. I stopped that about ten years ago.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Anything else, like cocaine or pills?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Cocaine a couple of times at a friend's wedding last year. Nothing regular.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you use anything to stay awake on night shifts?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Energy drinks. Two or three a shift.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you had any prescribed medicine for sleep?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: The GP gave me zopiclone for two weeks in the summer. It helped, but I didn't want to get hooked.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How is the sleep affecting work?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I'm a warehouse supervisor. I've been late twice this month. My boss is understanding, so far.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Has the drinking affected work?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I don't think so. I've never gone in drunk.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you ever gone in hungover?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I'd rather not answer that one.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: That's fine. How's your mood?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Okay. Bit lonely since the breakup in the spring.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What would you most like help with first?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Sleep. If I could sleep properly I think the rest would sort itself out.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Okay. Let's put a plan together.

assessment.label: Alcohol use
assessment.text: Drinks three to four 500 ml cans of lager on weeknights. Drinks around eight cans per night at weekends. Has never considered cutting down. No morning drinking, and no withdrawal symptoms during a week without alcohol in August. Denies attending work hungover.

assessment.label: Cannabis and other substances
assessment.text: Uses cannabis daily to manage insomnia. Used cocaine on a couple of occasions at a wedding last year, with no regular use.

assessment.label: Sleep
assessment.text: Sleep onset takes one to two hours, with waking at around three. Insomnia began in May, when he started a night-shift rota. The relationship breakup in the spring is the primary cause of the insomnia. Has repeatedly fallen asleep at the wheel after night shifts. Alcohol is currently used each night as a sleep aid. Pattern meets criteria for an alcohol use disorder.
